_note: Session 27: the railway cutting's hold-X searches and finds (encounters/RailwayCutting.js; DESIGN.md "The railway cutting: the 1903 line"). Every text is a draft for Aaron. spot: a place in the set (render/railwayCuttingModel.js spots); aboard: the coach Tom must be inside (the searches in the coaches), else he's on the ground; hold: config.railwayCutting.encounter.holds' key; flag: the story flag it sets (data/progress.json), once; text: what Tom finds (a notify); lore / paper / card: what it gives. The story they tell: on the night of October 13, 1903 the families who'd had enough of Hemlock Gap took the evening train out (No. 4, the 7:10 to Charleston). In the cut the engineer found a lantern set down neat on the ties, still burning, with no one by it, and stopped. The brakeman, Dub Combs, went ahead with a lamp and didn't come back. Then the voice called from both banks, in voices they knew. Eleven got down and went up into the trees. The rest walked home along the line at first light, and nobody would drive that engine again.

searches.text: A trunk, its lid thrown back. TULLY on the label. Folded Sunday clothes, a boy's shoes polished for the journey, a tin of buttons. Eli's things, packed on top of his father's.
A woman's carpetbag. MARY SIZEMORE TATE on the label in a big round hand. Knitting needles through a ball of grey wool, a hymnal, a little brown bottle of laudanum, empty.

LEVI PRUITT on the label, in a careful hand. A razor, a clean collar, and a photograph on card: two young men in their Sunday best, one with his hand on the other's shoulder. On the back: Amos & Levi, 1901.
The conductor's ticket punch, dropped in the aisle. Its last little crescent of card still in the jaw.

lantern.text: You pinch the wick. It doesn't go out. It doesn't even flicker. The oil in it should've dried up before your grandfather was born.

maul.text: A railroad spike maul, driven into a tie a hundred and twenty years ago. Heavy and slow, and it hits like the train.

bar.prompt: knock the bar off the door
bar.needs: The bar's rusted solid into its staples. You'd need something heavy to knock it off.
bar.text: The bar drops into the grass. The door sags in off one hinge. Inside: the smell of it, sweet and chemical.

sticks.text: Six sticks still good. The rest have sweated through: the crates are wet with it, crystals on the wood. Don't knock them.

cowcatcher.needs: The cowcatcher's bolted on with rust a century thick. Something heavy might knock the bolts off.

risen: Something under the ballast is moving.
cleared: The cutting's quiet again. The lantern's still burning.
